pattern: The X should first test A because ...
example: The school should first test a quiet zone because the strongest criteria are reducing a documented access barrier and producing clear evidence within a short period.
usage_note: 最初の一文で「何を先にやるか」と理由の核を同時に出す
caution: first test と書くと『まず試す』になり、断定的な『導入すべき』より安全

pattern: The X should prioritize A because it directly addresses ...
example: The school should prioritize Option B because it directly addresses a documented scheduling barrier and can be tested within one term without requiring students to own special equipment.
usage_note: 複数案から一つを選ぶ答え方。理由は判断基準に結びつける
caution: directly addresses の後ろは本文・表にある具体的な barrier にする

pattern: A X should consider -ing ...
example: A city should consider extending the hours of some public parks especially where many residents cannot use them during the day.
usage_note: 断定を避けた提案の書き出し。consider で『検討すべき』にとどめる
caution: consider だけでは弱いので、直後に理由か条件を置く

pattern: The X should test A rather than (immediately) B
example: The center should test a confirmation system rather than immediately imposing strict booking limits or large fees.
usage_note: 本命案と退ける案を一文で対比する
caution: 退ける案は『完全に否定』ではなく immediately の対象にして柔らかくする

pattern: A suggests that ... but it does not show that ...
example: The trial suggests that students value the homework-help session before major exams but it does not show that demand will remain high during ordinary weeks.
usage_note: 『分かったこと』と『言えないこと』を一文で分ける
caution: show と suggest の強さの差に注意。suggest=示唆、show=はっきり示す

pattern: The study shows that ... but this result does not prove that ...
example: The study shows that the method can save time under the tested conditions but this result does not prove that organizations will adopt it quickly.
usage_note: 結果の範囲(tested conditions)と、そこから先の主張を分ける
caution: prove は強い語。否定形で使うと言い過ぎを避けられる

pattern: Adoption may become more likely if ...
example: Adoption may become more likely if the method remains useful in real settings and if costs regulation training and compatibility do not create major barriers.
usage_note: 可能性を条件付きで述べる(may + more likely + if)
caution: will にすると断定になる。条件 if を必ず添える

pattern: ... would remain uncertain and would require evidence from ...
example: broader industry effects would remain uncertain and would require evidence from more organizations and settings.
usage_note: 分からないことを分からないと書き、必要な根拠まで示す
caution: uncertain と書くだけで終わらず『何が必要か』まで書くと答案が閉じる

pattern: A may not represent B
example: one month may not represent every season so the schedule should remain temporary until more evidence is available.
usage_note: データの代表性の限界を述べる
caution: cannot ではなく may not にして過度な否定を避ける

pattern: However, ... may ..., so the X should ...
example: However some users may forget to confirm so the center should send one reminder.
usage_note: 懸念を出し、その対処をすぐ続ける(限定→行動)
caution: 懸念だけで終わると答案が弱くなる。必ず so で対処に繋ぐ

pattern: The main limitation is that ... so ...
example: The main limitation is that group-work space would become smaller so the school should monitor congestion as well as quiet-zone use during a four-week pilot before making the change permanent.
usage_note: 案の最大の弱点を一つだけ挙げ、監視する指標に繋ぐ
caution: limitation を複数並べず一つに絞る

pattern: The main uncertainty is that ... may not become ...
example: The main uncertainty is that survey interest may not become actual attendance.
usage_note: 予測と実際の行動のずれを限界として示す
caution: uncertainty は『分からない点』。『問題点』とは区別する

pattern: The current X is limited so ...
example: The current survey is limited so a short follow-up test would provide stronger evidence before the library commits additional staff and operating costs.
usage_note: 現在の根拠の弱さを認め、追加の根拠を提案する
caution: limited の理由(何が足りないか)を前の文で示しておく

pattern: A could still help ... so it should not be abandoned
example: A printed guide could still help people understand the different alert methods so it should not be abandoned.
usage_note: 選ばなかった案にも価値を認める(譲歩)
caution: 譲歩だけで終わらせず、次の文で主張に戻る

pattern: the policy should not be identical in every ... because ...
example: However the policy should not be identical in every location because noise and staffing needs differ.
usage_note: 一律ルールを避ける理由(条件の違い)を述べる
caution: because の後は具体的な違いの種類を2つ程度挙げる

pattern: A directly addresses a documented ... barrier
example: The school should prioritize Option B because it directly addresses a documented scheduling barrier
usage_note: 『資料で確認できる問題に直接対応する』という選択理由の型
caution: documented は本文・表に根拠がある場合だけ使う

pattern: ... because these measures answer different questions
example: Public-service evaluation should distinguish among use user experience and reach because these measures answer different questions and may produce different results.
usage_note: 区別する理由を『問いが違うから』で説明する
caution: may produce で『結果が違い得る』と控えめに書く

pattern: Doing A would release ... while allowing ...
example: Requiring confirmation two days before use would release bookings that people no longer need while allowing genuine multi-date users to keep theirs.
usage_note: 対策の仕組み(メカニズム)を一文で説明する
caution: while で『副作用が小さい理由』を同時に示せる

pattern: The X could begin with ... and monitor A B and C
example: The city could begin with two later evenings each week and monitor use complaints and costs.
usage_note: 試行で何を観察するかを列挙して計画を具体化する
caution: 観察項目は3つ以内。目的に関係するものだけにする

pattern: run the trial for N months and record ...
example: The city should run the trial for three months and record attendance completed registrations and whether participants had previously been unable to use daytime support.
usage_note: 期間と記録項目をセットで示す
caution: 期間と指標がないと『検証』にならない

pattern: compare A with B to test whether ...
example: The city should therefore run the Sunday opening for two months and compare new-user numbers repeat use and actual attendance with the survey prediction.
usage_note: 予測と結果の比較で仮説を検証する計画を書く
caution: compare A with B。A to B ではなく with が基本

pattern: Option A may ..., but it mainly ...
example: Option A may attract more users but it mainly adds convenience to a service that many students can already access.
usage_note: 退ける案の長所を認めつつ、本質的な弱点を述べる
caution: may で長所を認め、mainly で弱点の中心を絞る

pattern: A is slightly more expensive, yet ... justifies the extra cost
example: Option B is slightly more expensive than the cheapest choice yet the stronger connection to the school's access goal justifies the extra cost.
usage_note: 費用面の不利を認めて、目的との整合で正当化する
caution: cost の不利を隠さずに書くと信頼性が上がる

pattern: Adding A might serve ... but it would not help ...
example: Adding more group tables might serve many students but it would not help those who currently leave because they cannot study quietly.
usage_note: 別案が助ける人と助けない人を分けて比べる
caution: would not help の対象(those who ...)を具体的に書く

pattern: more consistent with A than B
example: which is more consistent with unmet schedule access than Option A's already-busy central room.
usage_note: データがどちらの説明により合うかを比べる
caution: consistent with は『矛盾しない』。因果の証明にはならない

pattern: This would show whether ...
example: This would show whether predictable basketball access reduces conflict without removing too much flexibility.
usage_note: 試行で何が分かるかを結論文にする
caution: show whether + 疑問の内容。『分かる』ことを断定しない

pattern: That evidence would show whether ... is a significant barrier
example: That evidence would show whether access hours are a significant barrier.
usage_note: 収集する根拠が判断にどう使えるかを書く
caution: would を使い、まだ結果が出ていないことを示す

pattern: before the X commits ... / before the rule becomes permanent
example: This limited follow-up would show whether the service has regular value before the school commits staff time to a permanent weekly program.
usage_note: 恒久化の前に検証する理由を書いて結論を閉じる
caution: before の後に『何を決める前か』を明示する

pattern: This would make the ... more evidence-based
example: This would make the final funding choice more evidence-based.
usage_note: 検証の意義を一文で締める
caution: 締めの一文は短くし、新しい論点を足さない

pattern: This approach would preserve ... while keeping ... easy to reverse
example: This approach would preserve access while keeping the trial easy to reverse.
usage_note: 提案の利点(守るもの)とリスク管理(元に戻せる)で締める
caution: easy to reverse は小規模試行を勧める答案で使いやすい
